jobs.title: Director of Technology (Remote from anywhere in CO)
jobs.description:
Department Information

Together, we innovate for a stronger Colorado

The work of employees at the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) is challenging and diverse because the needs of agencies, customers and Coloradans constantly evolve. But our focus never changes: improve the lives of all Coloradans through innovation and collaboration. We're building one of the nation's leading government IT organizations by reimagining how we support agencies, building first-of-their-kind applications, and creating an inclusive, collaborative culture, together. Join us in the important work of providing equitable access to services.

Watch this video to learn more about how we're Serving People. Serving Colorado.

Description Of Job

IMPORTANT NOTE:

Please review your application to ensure completion. For the most equitable applicant experience, OIT’s hiring team considers only the contents of your application to review your qualifications. Please do not include any attachments (such as resume or cover letter) with your application as these items are not used by OIT’s hiring team.

The Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology is in the middle of a transformation worth joining. We're building cross-functional pod teams that partner directly with agencies to design, deliver, and continuously improve services that work for Coloradans. Good government depends on technology that works. And OIT exists to make that true for every Coloradan. The State of Colorado is seeking a Director, Technology to help build the next generation of public services. We're looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers in service of the public.

The Director, Technology is the Leader in OIT’s agency service model. You will determine the appropriate approach in working with OIT and Agency executives in aligning and implementing OIT and agency business needs. This position operates proactively as a strategic partner, embedding in agency planning before problems surface, rather than reactively as a service provider. You will build credibility with agency leadership quickly and maintain it through demonstrated delivery. The role oversees technology used to support all aspects of any supported agency's technology needs and collaborates with agency leadership as a strategic partner to provide in-depth technical expertise in support of business decisions.

What You'll Do...

Communicate and translate between technology initiatives and mission requirements with senior agency stakeholders, including Executive Director, CFO, and program leads.
Facilitate discussions with agency stakeholders and operational staff to identify competing priorities and elicit clear decisions.
Develop and maintain a living technology roadmap that is focused on agency priorities, which can be shifted to meet changing needs.
Oversee advisory teams as a matrixed leader coordinating agency technology portfolios.
Monitor vendor contract performance in terms of agreed outcomes and escalate failure to deliver on standards.
Identify, assess, and communicate technology risk effectively to non-technical agency leaders.
Understand and align OIT services with customer expectations to achieve high satisfaction.
Develop outcome-based performance agreements with agency stakeholders that define success in terms of mission impact and constituent benefit, not system availability or ticket volume.
Drive compliance with enterprise architecture standards (EA), while maintaining focus on agency missions and program needs; flag exceptions and engage OIT’s EA function.
Implement user centricity, agile, product ownership, modular procurement, and continuous delivery at conceptual and operational levels.
Work with cross-functional teams at agency and OIT to efficiently navigate State governance and procurement laws, considering factors such as SOO vs SOW, as well as T&M Structures.
Develop, drive, and hold staff accountable to team expectations tied to outcomes rather than activity metrics.
Conduct regular 1:1s and performance conversations that are developmental and coaching-oriented, which provide direct, honest feedback and accountability to team members. Build an environment where team members surface problems early rather than hiding them.
Provide proactive intervention to mitigate issues arising from workload, skill-gaps, etc., that are not dependent upon performance review cycles.
Conduct human resource management activities such as developing performance plans, and approving performance reviews; oversee disciplinary/corrective, and separation actions.
Coordinate with the OIT HR team to drive recruitment and selection processes that consider user-centered outcomes, and candidate experience.

What You Bring...

Ability to speak credibly to an agency's Executive Director, CFO, and program leads, to translate between technology and mission. This includes the ability to identify, assess and communicate technology risks to non-technical audiences.
Ability to navigate complex political dynamics, while maintaining focus on outcomes.
Ability to influence agency program staff and political leadership through collaboration and complex relationship management.
Ability to develop and maintain a multi-year roadmap that aligns technology investment to mission priorities
Ability to manage budget and resources, and influence thinking in regards to technology investment.
Ability to set individual and team performance expectations tied to outcomes, conduct developmental performance conversations, and navigate performance issues constructively across a cross-functional team of specialists.
Ability to manage across disciplines — providing meaningful feedback and accountability to team members — without needing to be a practitioner in each craft.
Ability to quickly understand state agency planning, budget, and decision-making processes, including budget cycles, legislative constraints, and executive branch governance
Knowledge of enterprise architecture fundamentals sufficient to apply EA standards, flag exceptions, and engage meaningfully with OIT's EA function
Ability to apply modern software delivery approaches, including user centricity, agile, product ownership, modular procurement, and continuous delivery at a conceptual and operational level
Knowledge of State IT governance, procurement law, and vendor contracting in a government context.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions Of Employment & Appeal Rights

A wide salary range is posted for this position and any job offer is based upon a salary analysis to comply with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act. The salary analysis considers relevant experience, education, certifications, and state seniority as compared to others doing substantially similar work. While all offers are compliant with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, there is no guarantee an offer will be at the top of the posted range based on the salary analysis.

Minimum Qualifications

This is a skills-based job announcement. The required minimum qualifications and/or education (if substituting for the proven experience, knowledge, and skills), are as follows:

A minimum of eight (8) years of experience as a lead in the delivery of technology solutions, to include three (3) years experience managing cross-functional teams using iterative, user-centered methods.
A track record of working across disciplines — design, engineering, policy, or operations — to ship things that work for real people.

Substitutions

Additional appropriate education will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis, but cannot completely substitute for these qualifications.

Training or Certification related to the work assigned to the position will be assigned credit towards substitution for experience and/or education, but cannot completely substitute for these qualifications.

If the minimum qualifications include a degree requirement, additional appropriate paid or unpaid experience will substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.

Preferred Qualifications

Relevant certifications such as Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), Pragmatic Institute Product Management, PMP, or Professional Product Manager (PPM).
Experience working within a digital service agency or a government-adjacent technology firm, successfully translating mission-driven policy goals into actionable product backlogs.
Experience in modern procurement practices is highly desirable, with the ability to structure vendor requirements in a way that remains outcome-oriented and agile rather than locking the state into rigid, fixed-scope contracts
Background in User-Centered Design (UCD).

Conditions Of Employment

OIT employees must comply with any screening procedures in place at state agency locations where they might perform work.

A pre-employment background check will be conducted as part of the selection process. Post-employment background checks will be required for specific agencies as business needs dictate, which may include a polygraph exam, fingerprint-based criminal history search, reference checks, and a drug test.

This position may require travel within the specified geographic area, and to locations across the state as needed.

Supplemental Information

If this posting indicates “remote from anywhere in CO” in the title, periodic reporting to the primary state work location designated for the position is required. All remote work must be performed in Colorado.

While candidates from out of state will be considered for this role, the candidate selected for the position must relocate and reside in Colorado on the first day of their new position. A reasonable timeframe for relocation will be established on an individual basis, while considering business needs, and determining a start date.

We know it's important to support each other, and that means having a healthy balance of work and personal time. Visit our benefits to learn more about some of our great offerings that allow us all to have fulfilling lives.

Visit our How to Apply webpage to learn more about our application process and what to expect after you apply.

The State of Colorado strives to create a Colorado for All by building and maintaining workplaces that value and respect all Coloradans through a commitment to equal opportunity and hiring based on merit and fitness. The State is resolute in non-discriminatory practices in everything we do, including hiring, employment, and advancement opportunities.

The Governor's Office of Information Technology is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, our agency will assist individuals who have a disability with any reasonable accommodation requests related to employment, including completing the application process, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, participating in the employee selection process, and/or to perform essential job functions where the requested accommodation does not impose an undue hardship. If you have a disability and require reasonable accommodation to ensure you have a positive experience applying or interviewing for this position, please direct your inquiries to our ADA Coordinator at OIT_HR@state.co.us or call (303) 764-7900.

This posting may be used to fill multiple vacancies based upon business need.

The Governor's Office of Information Technology does NOT offer sponsored Visas for employment purposes.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, IT Project Delivery
jobs.description:
Forrest T. Jones & Company, Inc., and its affiliates (“FTJ”), provide insurance and insurance related services to clients, corporations, employers and individuals. These services include providing benefits through innovative life and health insurance plans, financial services, and customized insurance products for niche markets.

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, IT Project Delivery, leads a team of Project Managers, Business Analysts, and Quality Assurance Analysts responsible for delivering technology projects and product initiatives that support all business areas across FSL and FTJ. This role provides leadership and oversight for project execution, portfolio management, and delivery excellence.

The Senior Manager partners with business and technology leaders to manage project portfolios, support annual planning activities, and facilitate the prioritization of initiatives across the organization. This role aligns technology, resource capacity, budgets, and delivery timelines with strategic business objectives, ensuring resources are focused on the highest-value work. The Sr. Manager provides visibility into portfolio health, resource utilization, budget performance, and strategic alignment to enable informed decision-making and effective prioritization.

The Senior Manager develops and delivers executive and stakeholder reporting that provides transparency into current and planned initiatives, portfolio performance, resource capacity, financial performance, risks, and strategic outcomes.

In collaboration with IT Directors and Managers, the Senior Manager develops, monitors, and communicates enterprise IT resource plans to optimize capacity, balance demand, and support business priorities.

Additionally, the Senior Manager is accountable for forecasting, monitoring, and controlling project and portfolio costs, including hours, and for tracking actual versus planned costs. This role also provides enterprise-wide visibility into technology by consolidating, tracking, and reporting technology budgets and spending across all departments, including IT, to support effective financial planning and governance of technology-related expenditures.

Expectations

Develop and maintain a portfolio management framework that aligns technology and strategy, resource capacity, product roadmaps, and project delivery initiatives with the business’ priorities and organizational strategy.
Partner with IT Leadership to establish and continuously improve Agile Program Management practices that enable incremental delivery of business value and alignment with organizational priorities.
Collaborate with business and technology stakeholders to identify unmet business needs and opportunities, evaluate solution alternatives, and develop technology roadmaps that support strategic objectives.
Lead and mentor the team in building strong partnerships with business stakeholders to ensure business needs are understood, requirements are well defined and testable, and features are continuously built, tested, and delivered in agreed upon intervals and timelines.
Own project scope, budget, schedule, and delivery by engaging, tracking and supporting all IT and business stakeholders.
Proactively manage project and portfolio risks, issues, dependencies, assumptions, such that they are escalated and resolved to ensure successful delivery.
Work with IT Leadership to develop a Technology budget and track actual vs. projected cost on agreed upon intervals.
Coordinate with IT Leadership to develop and track IT resource capacity plans that determine how and when IT resource utilization in projects could be optimized to deliver business value.
Provide and communicate executive-level reporting, providing visibility into portfolio health, project status, resource utilization, financial impacts, risks, and alignment to the organization’s strategy.
Develop and mentor team to facilitate the next generation of leaders in Project Management, Portfolio Management, and IT Business Management.
Build strong relationships within the organization to understand business challenges and opportunities.

Competencies

Extensive experience with guiding teams that manage projects and programs following Agile Methodologies
Deep understanding of Resource Capacity planning
Proven track record of end-to-end ownership for planning, execution, and delivering results.
Build and mentor high performing teams that take ownership and accountability on assigned projects and meet deadline expectations.
Proven ability to influence stakeholders and build consensus, collaborating and communicating effectively across all levels of the organization.
Handle multiple competing initiatives/priorities and promptly toggle between them with ease.
Strong risk management skills, including identifying, assessing, mitigating, and communicating project and portfolio risks.
Customer Service oriented; ability to build strong partnerships with business stakeholders and IT leaders.
Excellent communication skills, capable of summarizing and concisely presenting ideas.
Willingness to explore, drive new ideas along with the ability to lead organizational change and drive adoption of new processes, methodologies, and technologies.
Experience in managing budgets over $5 million.

Requisites

Bachelor’s degree in management information systems, business, or related fields.
Minimum 10 years of experience leading technology projects, programs, portfolios, or PMO functions.
Minimum 8 years with project portfolio management experience with significant Agile Delivery experience
Proven record of excellent project delivery satisfying business expectations and executing the projects on time, with quality and under budget
Minimum of 5 years of people leadership experience, including performance management, coaching, and team development.
PMP Certification
Previous Insurance business experience desired
Highly proficient in Microsoft Office tools (Word, Excel, Visio, PowerPoint, Project), SharePoint, Azure DevOps, Power BI, and collaboration tools such as Teams

We offer comprehensive benefits to full-time employees including company-paid medical, STD, LTD and life insurance plus voluntary dental, vision, life/AD&D insurance, 401(k) with company matching, generous paid time off and much more.

We encourage applicants of all ages and experience, as we do not discriminate on the basis of an applicant’s age.

ALL OFFERS OF EMPLOYMENT ARE CONTINGENT UPON THE PASSING OF A DRUG SCREEN AND BACKGROUND CHECK.

jobs.title: IT Director, Payroll and Time & Attendance Technology
jobs.description:
IT Director, Payroll and Time & Attendance Technology – Remote

Remote, United States

Come build something that matters.

It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Sound like you? Join our top-notch team of approximately 43,500 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®, CUB CADET®, and HUSTLER®.

The Job:

As a IT Director, Payroll and Time & Attendance Technology, you’ll be part of our IT team working as a remote employee. You’ll get to:

Responsible partnering with HR & Payroll for the strategy, delivery, integration, support, and continuous improvement of enterprise platforms that enable payroll, workforce management, timekeeping, and attendance tracking across a global manufacturing organization. This role leads the technology capabilities supporting UKG Workforce Manager and ADP Payroll, and a breadth of technologies globally – ensuring reliable, compliant, and scalable operations for both hourly and salaried employee populations.
Partner closely with HR, Payroll, Operations, and external vendors to deliver solutions that support complex manufacturing environments. The role requires a strong blend of strategic leadership, operational discipline, systems integration expertise, and deep understanding of workforce management and payroll processes in a manufacturing setting.

Strategy and Leadership

Define and lead the technology roadmap for Payroll and Time & Attendance capabilities, aligned with enterprise HR, Payroll, and Global Supply Chain strategies – prioritizing initiatives that improve workforce productivity, compliance, and employee experience.
Serve as the senior IT leader for Payroll & Workforce Management solutions.
Lead and develop a team of IT professionals, including technical leads, analysts, architects, and support resources, across global and regional operations.
Establish governance, standards, and operating models for enhancements, releases, integrations, vendor management, and service delivery.

Delivery and Transformation

Oversee end-to-end delivery of lifecycle management of Payroll & Workforce Management capabilities, including implementations, upgrades, integrations, and process transformation initiatives.
Lead cross-functional efforts to improve time capture, attendance tracking, payroll accuracy, and workforce data flow across enterprise systems.
Ensure seamless integration between Workday, UKG, ADP, ERP, and connected systems, and reporting tools.
Drive standardization of global processes where appropriate while enabling plant-, country-, and region-specific requirements.

Manufacturing Operations Support

Ensure technology solutions effectively support manufacturing workforce needs.
Partner with operations and plant stakeholders to minimize payroll and timekeeping disruptions that could impact production or employee pay.
Support workforce processes that require high reliability during payroll close, shift changes, and period-end processing.

Operations and Service Management

Own production support and operational stability for payroll and time-related applications, with a strong focus on payroll-critical service windows.
Establish and monitor service levels, incident response, problem management, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement practices.
Ensure timely resolution of issues affecting employee pay, time capture, attendance exceptions, interfaces, and downstream reporting.
Oversee system health, interface monitoring, batch processing, reconciliation processes, and data quality controls.

Compliance, Controls, and Risk Management

Ensure systems support compliance with wage and hour laws, payroll tax and reporting requirements, labor regulations, collective bargaining considerations, and data privacy obligations across relevant jurisdictions.
Maintain strong controls over payroll and employee data, including access management, segregation of duties, audit logging, change control, and data retention.
Partner with HR, Payroll, Legal, and Cybersecurity teams to support audits and strengthen control environments.
Identify and mitigate operational, technology, compliance, and vendor risks related to payroll and timekeeping systems.

Architecture and Continuous Improvement

Provide leadership on solution architecture and integration design across the HR, timekeeping, and payroll technology landscape.
Drive automation, simplification, and process harmonization across system workflows.
Improve reporting and analytics capabilities related to labor, attendance, payroll accuracy, and workforce trends.
Evaluate new capabilities from platform vendors and recommend enhancements that improve scalability, compliance, and user experience..

The Person:

You love to learn and grow and be acknowledged for your valuable contributions. You’re not intimidated by innovation. Wouldn’t it be great if you could do your job and do a world of good? In fact, you embrace it. You also have:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or related field.
12+ years of experience in IT, with at least 8+ years of direct experience supporting and delivering Payroll, Time & Attendance, workforce management, and related HR technology capabilities.
5+ years of people management experience leading employees, including direct management analysts, architects, or application support professionals.
Demonstrated experience supporting manufacturing or industrial operations with large hourly employee populations.
Hands-on leadership experience with UKG Workforce Manager and ADP Payroll platforms.
Strong understanding of integrations across HCM, timekeeping, payroll, ERP, identity, and reporting ecosystems.
Experience leading large-scale implementations, upgrades, and support models in complex operational environments.
Strong knowledge of payroll processing, timekeeping, attendance, scheduling, labor rules, and compliance requirements.
Proven ability to manage vendors, budgets, project portfolios, and cross-functional stakeholder relationships.
Strong communication and executive stakeholder management skills.
Knowledge of SOX controls, audit requirements, and data privacy regulations.
Experience with middleware, APIs, and enterprise integration platforms.

The Details:

You’ll receive a competitive salary and a great benefits plan, including:

Medical, dental, life, vision, disability, 401(k), Employee Stock Purchase Plan, paid time off, and tuition reimbursement in addition to programs & benefits in support of your well-being.
Discounts on Stanley Black & Decker tools and other partner programs.

And More:

We want our company to be a place you’ll want to be – and stay. Being part of our team means you’ll get to:

Grow: Be part of our global company with 20+ brands to grow and develop your skills along multiple career paths.
Learn: Have access to a wealth of learning resources, including our digital learning portal.
Belong: Experience an awesome place to work, where we have mutual respect and a great appreciation for a wide range of perspectives and experiences.
Give Back: Help us continue to make positive changes locally and globally through volunteerism, giving back, and sustainable business practices.

What’s more, you’ll get that pride that comes from empowering makers, doers, protectors, and everyday heroes all over the world. We’re more than the #1 tools company. More than a driving force in outdoor power equipment. More than a global leader in industrial. We’re visionaries and innovators. As successful as we’ve been in the past, we have so much further to go. That’s where you come in. Join us!

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Technology Enablement
jobs.description:
Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP, one of the world’s leading global law firms with offices in strategic hubs of commerce, law, and government across North America, Asia, Europe, and the Middle East, is seeking to hire a Senior Manager, Technology Enablement.

The Senior Manager, Technology Enablement, serves as the business owner for the Practice Group's technology portfolio, ensuring the technology investments are effectively operationalized, adopted, optimized, and translated into measurable business value.

This role functions as an internal strategic consultant responsible for identifying operational opportunities, improving service delivery, leading enterprise initiatives, and maximizing the return on the Practice Group's technology investments.

Unlike traditional technology leadership positions focused on engineering or platform development, this role focuses on business enablement ensuring technology capabilities are fully leveraged through process optimization, stakeholder alignment, client engagement, operational consulting, and continuous improvement.

The Senior Manager partners directly with attorneys, clients, executive leadership, and operational teams to evaluate business needs, identify organizational blind spots, improve technology adoption, develop scalable service offerings, and lead strategic initiatives from concept through implementation.

Success in this position requires exceptional consulting, communication, operational strategy, project leadership, and change management skills, combined with deep experience within legal technology, eDiscovery, and professional services environments.

Maintaining an in-office presence is important to delivering our services through an integrated and collaborative work culture. This position will reside in any of our Boston, Washington DC, Philadelphia, Chicago, or San Francisco offices with a hybrid in-office/remote working schedule.

Responsibilities

Strategic Business Consulting

Serve as the operational business owner for current Practice Group technology investments.
Partner with attorneys, clients, and operational leaders to identify opportunities to enhance utilization of existing technology and services within the Operations business unit.
Evaluate operational effectiveness and recommend process and technology improvements.
Facilitate strategic planning sessions and provide recommendations to executive leadership.
Develop operational roadmaps aligned with business and technology objectives.

Technology Enablement

Drive adoption and maximize the business value of technology solutions, including RelOne and its expansive suite of tools in addition to other applications currently supported by the Operations team.
Evaluate technology utilization, identify underused capabilities, and develop strategies to increase adoption.
Identify opportunities to eliminate redundant technology and streamline the technology environment.

Strategic Initiative Leadership

Lead enterprise and Practice Group strategic initiatives from planning through implementation.
Develop business cases, ROI analyses, and executive presentations.
Facilitate steering committees and support organizational change management.
Coordinate with vendors and cross-functional stakeholders.
Provide PMO leadership and ensure initiatives remain aligned with business objectives.

Operational Excellence

Identify and implement opportunities for continuous improvement and operational efficiency.
Apply Lean principles, process mapping, and service delivery optimization to improve business processes.
Develop KPIs, governance frameworks, SOPs, and other tools to support consistent and effective operations.
Identify opportunities to streamline operations and recommend measures to improve efficiency and reduce expenses.

Client & Attorney Engagement

Partner with attorneys, clients, and internal stakeholders to understand business needs and provide technology consulting for core eDiscovery platforms.
Participate in client pitches and presentations as needed.
Conduct technology demonstrations and provide internal attorney education as needed.
Support service enablement and promote effective use of technology solutions.

Market & Technology Evaluation

Research emerging technologies, market trends, and industry best practices for core eDiscovery platforms to supplement existing tool suites currently supported by the Operations team.
Evaluate vendors and technology solutions through demonstrations and proof-of-concept initiatives.
Conduct ROI analysis, benchmarking, and technology assessments.
Develop recommendations to support technology investment and business decisions.

Leadership & Collaboration

Lead through influence and collaboration rather than direct authority.
Build consensus and foster strong relationships across business, technology, and operational teams.
Communicate effectively with executive leadership and stakeholders at all levels.
Support strategic planning, resource optimization, and organizational priorities.
Provide recommendations related to resources, budgets, and technology investments.
Additional responsibilities may be assigned as needed.

Measures of Success

Success In This Role Will Be Demonstrated Through

Increased technology adoption and utilization.
Reduced redundant or underutilized applications.
Successful delivery of strategic initiatives.
Improved operational KPIs and service delivery.
Increased attorney and client engagement and satisfaction.
Improved return on technology investments.
Increased operational efficiency and cost optimization.

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree (B.A.) from a four-year college or university and minimum of 15 years of relevant experience in a large law firm, legal service provider, and/or in-house corporate environment. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Strong legal technology knowledge, including Relativity and AI solutions.
Excellent communication, consulting, customer service, and interpersonal skills.
Strong leadership, executive presence, and ability to influence without direct authority.
Strategic thinking and business acumen, including budgeting, financial analysis, business case development, and portfolio management.
Strong project management, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to change, and work collaboratively.
Ability to analyze complex information and effectively communicate recommendations to senior leadership and clients.
PMP, Relativity Expert, or Lean Six Sigma certification is preferred but not required.

Qualified candidates must apply online by visiting our website at www.morganlewis.com and selecting “Careers.”

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Cybersecurity, AI SOC & Crisis Management - Remote
jobs.description:
Preference will be given to candidates residing in the Eastern or Central time zones.

As a Senior Manager, AI Security Operations & Crisis Management, you will lead the enterprise Cyber Incident Response Team (CIRT) and coordinate incidents through recovery and closure. You will advance AI-enabled operations and crisis readiness with Investigations, Threat Hunting & Forensics and enterprise partners.

What you will do:

Technical Responsibilities:

Lead global CIRT operations, including follow-the-sun coverage, escalation, containment, recovery, closure, and continuity during outages.

new_jobs.description:
Department Information

Together, we innovate for a stronger Colorado

The work of employees at the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) is challenging and diverse because the needs of agencies, customers and Coloradans constantly evolve. But our focus never changes: improve the lives of all Coloradans through innovation and collaboration. We're building one of the nation's leading government IT organizations by reimagining how we support agencies, building first-of-their-kind applications, and creating an inclusive, collaborative culture, together. Join us in the important work of providing equitable access to services.

Watch this video to learn more about how we're Serving People. Serving Colorado.

Description Of Job

IMPORTANT NOTE:

Please review your application to ensure completion. For the most equitable applicant experience, OIT’s hiring team considers only the contents of your application to review your qualifications. Please do not include any attachments (such as resume or cover letter) with your application as these items are not used by OIT’s hiring team.

The Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology is in the middle of a transformation worth joining. We're building cross-functional pod teams that partner directly with agencies to design, deliver, and continuously improve services that work for Coloradans. Good government depends on technology that works. And OIT exists to make that true for every Coloradan. The State of Colorado is seeking a Director, Technology to help build the next generation of public services. We're looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers in service of the public.

The Director, Technology is the Leader in OIT’s agency service model. You will determine the appropriate approach in working with OIT and Agency executives in aligning and implementing OIT and agency business needs. This position operates proactively as a strategic partner, embedding in agency planning before problems surface, rather than reactively as a service provider. You will build credibility with agency leadership quickly and maintain it through demonstrated delivery. The role oversees technology used to support all aspects of any supported agency's technology needs and collaborates with agency leadership as a strategic partner to provide in-depth technical expertise in support of business decisions.

What You'll Do...

Communicate and translate between technology initiatives and mission requirements with senior agency stakeholders, including Executive Director, CFO, and program leads.
Facilitate discussions with agency stakeholders and operational staff to identify competing priorities and elicit clear decisions.
Develop and maintain a living technology roadmap that is focused on agency priorities, which can be shifted to meet changing needs.
Oversee advisory teams as a matrixed leader coordinating agency technology portfolios.
Monitor vendor contract performance in terms of agreed outcomes and escalate failure to deliver on standards.
Identify, assess, and communicate technology risk effectively to non-technical agency leaders.
Understand and align OIT services with customer expectations to achieve high satisfaction.
Develop outcome-based performance agreements with agency stakeholders that define success in terms of mission impact and constituent benefit, not system availability or ticket volume.
Drive compliance with enterprise architecture standards (EA), while maintaining focus on agency missions and program needs; flag exceptions and engage OIT’s EA function.
Implement user centricity, agile, product ownership, modular procurement, and continuous delivery at conceptual and operational levels.
Work with cross-functional teams at agency and OIT to efficiently navigate State governance and procurement laws, considering factors such as SOO vs SOW, as well as T&M Structures.
Develop, drive, and hold staff accountable to team expectations tied to outcomes rather than activity metrics.
Conduct regular 1:1s and performance conversations that are developmental and coaching-oriented, which provide direct, honest feedback and accountability to team members. Build an environment where team members surface problems early rather than hiding them.
Provide proactive intervention to mitigate issues arising from workload, skill-gaps, etc., that are not dependent upon performance review cycles.
Conduct human resource management activities such as developing performance plans, and approving performance reviews; oversee disciplinary/corrective, and separation actions.
Coordinate with the OIT HR team to drive recruitment and selection processes that consider user-centered outcomes, and candidate experience.

What You Bring...

Ability to speak credibly to an agency's Executive Director, CFO, and program leads, to translate between technology and mission. This includes the ability to identify, assess and communicate technology risks to non-technical audiences.
Ability to navigate complex political dynamics, while maintaining focus on outcomes.
Ability to influence agency program staff and political leadership through collaboration and complex relationship management.
Ability to develop and maintain a multi-year roadmap that aligns technology investment to mission priorities
Ability to manage budget and resources, and influence thinking in regards to technology investment.
Ability to set individual and team performance expectations tied to outcomes, conduct developmental performance conversations, and navigate performance issues constructively across a cross-functional team of specialists.
Ability to manage across disciplines — providing meaningful feedback and accountability to team members — without needing to be a practitioner in each craft.
Ability to quickly understand state agency planning, budget, and decision-making processes, including budget cycles, legislative constraints, and executive branch governance
Knowledge of enterprise architecture fundamentals sufficient to apply EA standards, flag exceptions, and engage meaningfully with OIT's EA function
Ability to apply modern software delivery approaches, including user centricity, agile, product ownership, modular procurement, and continuous delivery at a conceptual and operational level
Knowledge of State IT governance, procurement law, and vendor contracting in a government context.

Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions Of Employment & Appeal Rights

A wide salary range is posted for this position and any job offer is based upon a salary analysis to comply with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act. The salary analysis considers relevant experience, education, certifications, and state seniority as compared to others doing substantially similar work. While all offers are compliant with the Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, there is no guarantee an offer will be at the top of the posted range based on the salary analysis.

Minimum Qualifications

This is a skills-based job announcement. The required minimum qualifications and/or education (if substituting for the proven experience, knowledge, and skills), are as follows:

A minimum of eight (8) years of experience as a lead in the delivery of technology solutions, to include three (3) years experience managing cross-functional teams using iterative, user-centered methods.
A track record of working across disciplines — design, engineering, policy, or operations — to ship things that work for real people.

Substitutions

Additional appropriate education will substitute for the required experience on a year-for-year basis, but cannot completely substitute for these qualifications.

Training or Certification related to the work assigned to the position will be assigned credit towards substitution for experience and/or education, but cannot completely substitute for these qualifications.

If the minimum qualifications include a degree requirement, additional appropriate paid or unpaid experience will substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.

Preferred Qualifications

Relevant certifications such as Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), Pragmatic Institute Product Management, PMP, or Professional Product Manager (PPM).
Experience working within a digital service agency or a government-adjacent technology firm, successfully translating mission-driven policy goals into actionable product backlogs.
Experience in modern procurement practices is highly desirable, with the ability to structure vendor requirements in a way that remains outcome-oriented and agile rather than locking the state into rigid, fixed-scope contracts
Background in User-Centered Design (UCD).

Conditions Of Employment

OIT employees must comply with any screening procedures in place at state agency locations where they might perform work.

A pre-employment background check will be conducted as part of the selection process. Post-employment background checks will be required for specific agencies as business needs dictate, which may include a polygraph exam, fingerprint-based criminal history search, reference checks, and a drug test.

This position may require travel within the specified geographic area, and to locations across the state as needed.

Supplemental Information

If this posting indicates “remote from anywhere in CO” in the title, periodic reporting to the primary state work location designated for the position is required. All remote work must be performed in Colorado.

While candidates from out of state will be considered for this role, the candidate selected for the position must relocate and reside in Colorado on the first day of their new position. A reasonable timeframe for relocation will be established on an individual basis, while considering business needs, and determining a start date.

Partner with IT Leadership to establish and continuously improve Agile Program Management practices that enable incremental delivery of business value and alignment with organizational priorities.

Build strong relationships within the organization to understand business challenges and opportunities.

Extensive experience with guiding teams that manage projects and programs following Agile Methodologies
Deep understanding of Resource Capacity planning
Proven track record of end-to-end ownership for planning, execution, and delivering results.

Proven ability to influence stakeholders and build consensus, collaborating and communicating effectively across all levels of the organization.
Handle multiple competing initiatives/priorities and promptly toggle between them with ease.
Strong risk management skills, including identifying, assessing, mitigating, and communicating project and portfolio risks.
Customer Service oriented; ability to build strong partnerships with business stakeholders and IT leaders.

Remote, United States

Come build something that matters.

It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Sound like you? Join our top-notch team of approximately 43,500 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®, CUB CADET®, and HUSTLER®.

The Job:

As a IT Director, Payroll and Time & Attendance Technology, you’ll be part of our IT team working as a remote employee. You’ll get to:

Responsible partnering with HR & Payroll for the strategy, delivery, integration, support, and continuous improvement of enterprise platforms that enable payroll, workforce management, timekeeping, and attendance tracking across a global manufacturing organization. This role leads the technology capabilities supporting UKG Workforce Manager and ADP Payroll, and a breadth of technologies globally – ensuring reliable, compliant, and scalable operations for both hourly and salaried employee populations.
Partner closely with HR, Payroll, Operations, and external vendors to deliver solutions that support complex manufacturing environments. The role requires a strong blend of strategic leadership, operational discipline, systems integration expertise, and deep understanding of workforce management and payroll processes in a manufacturing setting.

Strategy and Leadership

Define and lead the technology roadmap for Payroll and Time & Attendance capabilities, aligned with enterprise HR, Payroll, and Global Supply Chain strategies – prioritizing initiatives that improve workforce productivity, compliance, and employee experience.
Serve as the senior IT leader for Payroll & Workforce Management solutions.
Lead and develop a team of IT professionals, including technical leads, analysts, architects, and support resources, across global and regional operations.
Establish governance, standards, and operating models for enhancements, releases, integrations, vendor management, and service delivery.

Delivery and Transformation

Oversee end-to-end delivery of lifecycle management of Payroll & Workforce Management capabilities, including implementations, upgrades, integrations, and process transformation initiatives.
Lead cross-functional efforts to improve time capture, attendance tracking, payroll accuracy, and workforce data flow across enterprise systems.
Ensure seamless integration between Workday, UKG, ADP, ERP, and connected systems, and reporting tools.
Drive standardization of global processes where appropriate while enabling plant-, country-, and region-specific requirements.

Manufacturing Operations Support

Ensure technology solutions effectively support manufacturing workforce needs.
Partner with operations and plant stakeholders to minimize payroll and timekeeping disruptions that could impact production or employee pay.
Support workforce processes that require high reliability during payroll close, shift changes, and period-end processing.

Operations and Service Management

Own production support and operational stability for payroll and time-related applications, with a strong focus on payroll-critical service windows.
Establish and monitor service levels, incident response, problem management, root cause analysis, and continuous improvement practices.
Ensure timely resolution of issues affecting employee pay, time capture, attendance exceptions, interfaces, and downstream reporting.
Oversee system health, interface monitoring, batch processing, reconciliation processes, and data quality controls.

Compliance, Controls, and Risk Management

Ensure systems support compliance with wage and hour laws, payroll tax and reporting requirements, labor regulations, collective bargaining considerations, and data privacy obligations across relevant jurisdictions.
Maintain strong controls over payroll and employee data, including access management, segregation of duties, audit logging, change control, and data retention.
Partner with HR, Payroll, Legal, and Cybersecurity teams to support audits and strengthen control environments.
Identify and mitigate operational, technology, compliance, and vendor risks related to payroll and timekeeping systems.

Architecture and Continuous Improvement

Provide leadership on solution architecture and integration design across the HR, timekeeping, and payroll technology landscape.
Drive automation, simplification, and process harmonization across system workflows.
Improve reporting and analytics capabilities related to labor, attendance, payroll accuracy, and workforce trends.
Evaluate new capabilities from platform vendors and recommend enhancements that improve scalability, compliance, and user experience..

The Person:

new_jobs.title: Senior Manager, Technology Enablement
new_jobs.description:
Morgan, Lewis & Bockius LLP, one of the world’s leading global law firms with offices in strategic hubs of commerce, law, and government across North America, Asia, Europe, and the Middle East, is seeking to hire a Senior Manager, Technology Enablement.

The Senior Manager, Technology Enablement, serves as the business owner for the Practice Group's technology portfolio, ensuring the technology investments are effectively operationalized, adopted, optimized, and translated into measurable business value.

This role functions as an internal strategic consultant responsible for identifying operational opportunities, improving service delivery, leading enterprise initiatives, and maximizing the return on the Practice Group's technology investments.

Unlike traditional technology leadership positions focused on engineering or platform development, this role focuses on business enablement ensuring technology capabilities are fully leveraged through process optimization, stakeholder alignment, client engagement, operational consulting, and continuous improvement.

The Senior Manager partners directly with attorneys, clients, executive leadership, and operational teams to evaluate business needs, identify organizational blind spots, improve technology adoption, develop scalable service offerings, and lead strategic initiatives from concept through implementation.

Success in this position requires exceptional consulting, communication, operational strategy, project leadership, and change management skills, combined with deep experience within legal technology, eDiscovery, and professional services environments.

Maintaining an in-office presence is important to delivering our services through an integrated and collaborative work culture. This position will reside in any of our Boston, Washington DC, Philadelphia, Chicago, or San Francisco offices with a hybrid in-office/remote working schedule.

Responsibilities

Strategic Business Consulting

Serve as the operational business owner for current Practice Group technology investments.
Partner with attorneys, clients, and operational leaders to identify opportunities to enhance utilization of existing technology and services within the Operations business unit.
Evaluate operational effectiveness and recommend process and technology improvements.
Facilitate strategic planning sessions and provide recommendations to executive leadership.
Develop operational roadmaps aligned with business and technology objectives.

Technology Enablement

Drive adoption and maximize the business value of technology solutions, including RelOne and its expansive suite of tools in addition to other applications currently supported by the Operations team.
Evaluate technology utilization, identify underused capabilities, and develop strategies to increase adoption.
Identify opportunities to eliminate redundant technology and streamline the technology environment.

Strategic Initiative Leadership

Lead enterprise and Practice Group strategic initiatives from planning through implementation.
Develop business cases, ROI analyses, and executive presentations.
Facilitate steering committees and support organizational change management.
Coordinate with vendors and cross-functional stakeholders.
Provide PMO leadership and ensure initiatives remain aligned with business objectives.

Operational Excellence

Identify and implement opportunities for continuous improvement and operational efficiency.
Apply Lean principles, process mapping, and service delivery optimization to improve business processes.
Develop KPIs, governance frameworks, SOPs, and other tools to support consistent and effective operations.
Identify opportunities to streamline operations and recommend measures to improve efficiency and reduce expenses.

Client & Attorney Engagement

Partner with attorneys, clients, and internal stakeholders to understand business needs and provide technology consulting for core eDiscovery platforms.
Participate in client pitches and presentations as needed.
Conduct technology demonstrations and provide internal attorney education as needed.
Support service enablement and promote effective use of technology solutions.

Market & Technology Evaluation

Research emerging technologies, market trends, and industry best practices for core eDiscovery platforms to supplement existing tool suites currently supported by the Operations team.
Evaluate vendors and technology solutions through demonstrations and proof-of-concept initiatives.
Conduct ROI analysis, benchmarking, and technology assessments.
Develop recommendations to support technology investment and business decisions.

Leadership & Collaboration

Lead through influence and collaboration rather than direct authority.
Build consensus and foster strong relationships across business, technology, and operational teams.
Communicate effectively with executive leadership and stakeholders at all levels.
Support strategic planning, resource optimization, and organizational priorities.
Provide recommendations related to resources, budgets, and technology investments.
Additional responsibilities may be assigned as needed.

Measures of Success

Success In This Role Will Be Demonstrated Through

Increased technology adoption and utilization.
Reduced redundant or underutilized applications.
Successful delivery of strategic initiatives.
Improved operational KPIs and service delivery.
Increased attorney and client engagement and satisfaction.
Improved return on technology investments.
Increased operational efficiency and cost optimization.

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree (B.A.) from a four-year college or university and minimum of 15 years of relevant experience in a large law firm, legal service provider, and/or in-house corporate environment. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Strong legal technology knowledge, including Relativity and AI solutions.
Excellent communication, consulting, customer service, and interpersonal skills.
Strong leadership, executive presence, and ability to influence without direct authority.
Strategic thinking and business acumen, including budgeting, financial analysis, business case development, and portfolio management.
Strong project management, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage competing priorities, adapt to change, and work collaboratively.
Ability to analyze complex information and effectively communicate recommendations to senior leadership and clients.
PMP, Relativity Expert, or Lean Six Sigma certification is preferred but not required.

Qualified candidates must apply online by visiting our website at www.morganlewis.com and selecting “Careers.”

For positions in Washington, DC, and Boston, MA, the salary range for this position is: 143,000.00- $228,800.00

For positions in Chicago, IL, the salary range for this position is: $136,800.00 - $218,850.00

For positions in San Francisco, CA, the salary range for this position is: $155,500.00 - $248,725.00

The base salary or hourly wage range for this position will be determined during the interview process and will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to prior experience, relevant expertise, current business needs, and market factors. The final salary or hourly wages offered may be outside of this range based on other reasons and individual circumstances. Additionally, salary or hourly wages may be only part of the total compensation package. The total compensation package for this position may also include a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment. If hired, the employee will be in an "at-will position" and the firm reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation or benefit program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, firm or individual department/team performance, and market factors.
